read.title: Read the plan
read.instruction: Read, in this order, before writing any code: CLAUDE.md at the repository root; the implementation plan for this release (Spec/plans/<release>.md when the repo has it, otherwise the plan note the user named); the open tasks of the matching project in the Obsidian vault when a vault path is configured in CLAUDE.md; any acceptance criteria for the scope given in the arguments. Then write a scope statement into the Kata state file: the PR's goal in one sentence, the files you expect to touch, the acceptance criteria as a checklist, and what is explicitly out of scope. Print the scope statement to the user. Do not write code in this step.

implement.title: Implement the scope
implement.instruction: Implement only what the scope statement lists, following the architecture rules in CLAUDE.md and the plan's file layout. Add or update tests alongside the code. Do not add a dependency, change a public contract, or touch files outside the scope without asking the user in plain text first. Do not commit in this step.

review.title: Full self-review
review.instruction: Review the whole change yourself: run git diff against the base branch and read every touched file in full. Do not invoke any review skill, slash command or subagent for this. Produce a numbered issue list covering correctness, missing or weak tests, architecture-rule violations (dependency direction, banned imports, logging rules), naming and API consistency, leftover debug code or TODOs, and documentation or localisation gaps. Each issue names the file and line, a severity (high, medium or low) and what to change. Record every issue in the Kata state file's issues list with status open, print the list, and end the step's note with the count. An empty list is a valid result only after you have read every touched file.

fix.title: Fix every issue
fix.instruction: Fix every open issue in the Kata state file's issues list, one at a time. Before each, set the step's activity to the issue you are on; after each, mark it fixed (or skipped with the reason in the chat) and update the step's progress to fixed out of the total. When an issue needs a product or design decision, ask the user in plain text (never a form or multiple-choice widget), wait for the answer, then continue. After fixing, run the review step once more on the new diff and add anything new it finds; repeat fix and review until no issue is open.

verify.title: Lint, tests, architecture check
verify.instruction: Run the project's checks. With a mise.toml present run `mise run lint`, `mise run test` and `mise run arch:check` (skip a task that does not exist and say so). Without mise, run the equivalents named in CLAUDE.md or the project's standard tooling. Keep the step's activity on the check that is running and its progress at checks passed out of checks run. Add each failure you cannot fix at once to the issues list. Fix failures and rerun until everything passes. Do not continue to the next step while any check fails; if a failure cannot be fixed inside the scope, stop and report it to the user with the output.

commit.title: Commit without trailers
commit.instruction: Stage only the files in scope (never `git add -A` blindly; list what is staged). Commit with a Conventional Commits message: `type(scope): summary` under 72 characters, a blank line, then a body that says what changed and why. The message carries no trailers of any kind: no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with, no Signed-off-by. The Kata hook blocks a commit that carries one; rewrite the message rather than bypassing the hook.

acceptance.title: Acceptance criteria and TODOs
acceptance.instruction: Compare the result with the scope statement from the read step. For each acceptance criterion write met or not met with the evidence (file, test name, command output), keeping the step's progress at criteria met out of the total. List any TODO or task item from the plan that this PR was meant to close and whether it is closed. If anything is not met, add it to the issues list and return to the implement step for that item, then run the following steps again. When a vault or task tracker is configured in CLAUDE.md, close the matching task when CLAUDE.md says to: on acceptance (now), or on merge (leave it open and say it closes when the pull request merges). With no rule in CLAUDE.md, close it on merge. Record the table in the state file.

pr.title: Open the pull request
pr.instruction: Push the branch and open the pull request with `gh pr create`. Title: the commit summary. Body, in this order: `## Summary` with three to six bullets of what changed; `## Description` with why the change is made, the design decisions taken, and what a reviewer should read first; `## Testing` with the commands run and their results; `## Checklist` with each acceptance criterion as a ticked or unticked box. No attribution footer or generated-by line. Print the PR URL, then mark the Kata run finished in the state file.

pr-read.title: Read the pull request
pr-read.instruction: Find the pull request named in the arguments (a number or a URL; with neither, the open pull request for the current branch). Run gh pr view with its title, body, author, base and head branches, linked issues and state, gh pr checks for CI, and gh pr diff for the change. Read the repository's CLAUDE.md and any CONTRIBUTING file: their rules are part of the review. If you reviewed this pull request before, read that review (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews and its comments) and list the commits pushed since. Write the scope in one line: what the pull request says it does. Stop and say so if the pull request is closed, merged or cannot be found.

pr-review.title: Review every changed file
pr-review.instruction: Note the branch you are on, check out the pull request's head with gh pr checkout, and read every changed file in full, not only the diff hunks, plus the code that calls what changed. Do not invoke any review skill, slash command or subagent. Record each finding in the Kata state file's issues with the file, the line on the pull request's side of the diff, a one-line title and a severity on the review scale: major for a bug, data loss, a security or privacy problem, a broken API contract or migration, new behaviour without tests, or a rule in CLAUDE.md broken; minor for edge cases, error handling, a misleading name, a missing doc or translation, or a test that does not test what it says; nit for style, wording, ordering or a simpler way to write the same thing. On a re-review, carry over the earlier findings, mark the ones the new commits fixed as fixed, and raise new findings only on new code. Print the findings grouped by severity and end the step's note with the counts, such as 2 major, 1 minor, 3 nits. No findings is a valid result only after you have read every changed file. When you are done, switch back to the branch you were on.

pr-verdict.title: Decide the verdict
pr-verdict.instruction: Decide from the open findings: any major means request changes; minors without a major mean comment, unless the project's CLAUDE.md says to approve with comments; only nits, or nothing, means approve. Set the verdict in the Kata state file. Draft the review: a short summary of what the pull request does and how well, the verdict and why, then one inline comment per finding on its file and line, starting with major:, minor: or nit:, saying what to change and why. Nits are optional suggestions. Show the whole draft. Post nothing in this step.

pr-post.title: Post the review
pr-post.instruction: Post the review drafted in the previous step, as shown and approved, in one call: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews with body (the summary), event (APPROVE, COMMENT or REQUEST_CHANGES from the verdict) and comments (path, line, side RIGHT, body for each finding). If the pull request is the user's own, GitHub refuses APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES: post it as COMMENT and say so. A comment whose line is not part of the diff goes into the summary instead. Print the review's URL. To draft without posting, run the mode with --skip pr-post.

pr.name: PR implementation
pr.description: Read the plan, implement one PR's scope, self-review, fix, verify, commit without trailers, check acceptance, open an itemised PR.

review-pr.name: PR review
review-pr.description: Review someone's pull request: read it, review every changed file, sort findings into major, minor and nits, approve when only nits remain, request changes on any major, and post the review after you confirm.
